name: LCI INDUSTRIES

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That a -0.93% spread is too tight for a deal that has drawn a Second Request on a 1-versus-2 horizontal combination, so there IS a tradable opinion here - a merger-arbitrage short rather than a valuation long. If the market is pricing roughly 99% completion against a genuine antitrust challenge, the risk is mispriced and refusing to say so is itself a judgment.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: A credible standalone break price for LCII, against which the implied completion probability could be solved from the 1.2440-ratio value.
devils_advocate.already_visible: No, and this is the second consecutive pass at which it is not. The spread and the Second Request are both visible; the break price is not, and establishing it requires a standalone valuation of a cyclical RV supplier in a declining shipment year, which is exactly what this engine's inputs cannot deliver on this name. I had hoped the S-4 would help and it does not: as of 2026-10-13 it is still not effective, so the definitive joint proxy - which is where the background of the merger, the full condition set and the financial advisers' standalone analyses would sit - is not yet public. Worth recording that the thing which would settle the nominated question is a document that has not been filed, rather than one I failed to fetch.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The implied completion probability, for the same reason as last week. I also still have not read the S-4 itself, because it is not effective; the outside date of 2027-03-30 recorded on the PATK pass and the expected first-half-2027 close remain unconfirmed from a primary document. And I cannot assess how likely the DOJ is to demand divestitures, which is the whole question.

what_changed: Nothing material since this name was last researched on 2026-10-16, which is itself the finding. The Second Request remains the live event: the 8-K of 2026-10-13 confirms that on 2026-10-09 both LCI and Patrick received a request for additional information from the DOJ, extending the HSR waiting period until 30 days after both parties substantially comply. The Form S-4 (File No. 333-299100), filed by Patrick on 2026-09-23 and containing the preliminary joint proxy statement, had STILL NOT become effective as of 2026-10-13, and no shareholder vote is scheduled. The only new filing is the 2026-10-22 8-K, which is an item 7.01 announcement that third-quarter results will be released on 2026-11-05 - a scheduling notice, not news. The spread is essentially unchanged from the -0.87% recorded a week ago.
consensus_case: At $86.60 LCI Industries has no independent price: it is Patrick Industries multiplied by the contracted 1.2440 exchange ratio. Patrick closed at $70.27, which values LCII at $87.42, so the stock trades at a -0.93% spread to deal terms - and the two names' five-day returns are IDENTICAL at +3.1% each, with 21-day returns of +1.8% against +1.6% and 63-day of -15.3% against -16.4%. The market is expressing a view on whether an all-stock merger of the first and second largest suppliers of engineered components to the RV industry survives a Department of Justice review, not a view on recreational-vehicle cash flows. At roughly 99% implied completion it is paying a merger-arbitrage price.
base_case_rationale: No growth rate and no fair value are supplied, for the same reason as a week ago: the company has contracted to stop existing in its present form, so a standalone discounted cash flow does not describe anything. The mechanical inputs remain clean - implied interest rate 4.19%, D&A to capex 2.4x, add-back 7% of base, equity_now $1,431.8 million against equity_series[0] $1,360.8 million so no stale book, and a share count of 24,311,507 that reconciles to LCI's actual count - and that is precisely the point this name keeps making: nothing in the data is broken and the name is still unmodellable, because what is wrong is that the engine does not know the company is being acquired. The single flag raised, `possible_trough_cycle_base_newest_fcf_0.60x_oldest`, is true about the RV cycle (2026 North American wholesale shipment guidance was cut to 280,000-300,000 from 315,000-330,000, and the cash-flow series falls $465.0 million to $328.0 million to $278.3 million) and irrelevant to the valuation. The +250.0% gap at the 96.8th percentile of 125 Consumer Discretionary names is additionally void for a second, independent reason: the '+8.1% five-year revenue CAGR' baseline is measured from 2020, since revenue_series runs $4,122.0 million, $3,741.2 million, $3,784.8 million, $5,207.1 million, $4,472.7 million, $2,796.2 million - so it is anchored on the COVID trough while the actual peak of $5,207.1 million sits in 2022 and revenue is still 21% below it. That is the PATK artefact, and it would make the gap wrong even if there were no merger.
key_risks: The price is PATK x 1.2440, not a cash-flow opinion: actual ratio 1.2324 against the contracted 1.2440, a -0.93% spread, with five-day returns identical at +3.1% on both names
DOJ Second Request issued 2026-10-09 to both parties - a material antitrust escalation on a 1-versus-2 horizontal combination in RV components
The S-4 (File No. 333-299100) filed 2026-09-23 was still NOT effective as of 2026-10-13, and no shareholder vote is scheduled
The $94.2M reciprocal break fee is under 5% of market capitalisation and does not protect the equity if the deal breaks
The +8.1% baseline behind the +250% gap is measured from 2020's COVID-trough revenue of $2,796.2M; revenue peaked at $5,207.1M in 2022 and is still 21% below it
This transaction has now consumed four slots across four sessions (LCII 09-11, PATK 09-15, LCII 10-16, LCII 10-23) and PATK ranks at the 87.2nd percentile again today
